title: MPs get UNDP training on SDG and spending oversight
excerpt: Parliament and UNDP, with Swiss support, opened a two-day course for MPs on tracking SDG progress and public procurement.
content:
The Parliament Secretariat has started a two-day orientation for members of Parliament on overseeing progress on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the use of public money, UNDP Bangladesh said on 15 November. The course is supported by UNDP and Switzerland under UNDP's Strengthening Institutions, Policies and Services (SIPS) project.

The first day covers SDG progress and tools for parliamentary monitoring. The second covers public procurement rules, transparency and project management.

"It is not only the allocation of funds that matters," said Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad Bir Bikram. Chief Whip Nurul Islam Moni said: "Achieving development goals is closely linked to the proper use of public funds." Stephen Rodriques, UNDP Resident Representative, told MPs: "This is not a commitment that Bangladesh made to the United Nations."

Facilitators included Owais Parray, UNDP country economic adviser, Dr Monzur Hossain of the General Economics Division, Prof S M Abdul-Awal, principal coordinator for SDG affairs at the Prime Minister's Office, and Abu Sayed Md. Kamruzzaman, chief executive of the Bangladesh Public Procurement Authority.

Why it matters

Development spending is at a record low and Parliament has just relaxed procurement rules, so the quality of MPs' oversight matters. Accountability NGOs can use committee hearings and MPs' questions as a route to raise gaps in service delivery and spending.

What to watch

Whether parliamentary standing committees start holding regular hearings on SDG progress and development projects.
